# Copilot instructions for contract-generator

Java library that renders a Thymeleaf HTML contract into a PDF with **fillable AcroForm fields**
(via openhtmltopdf's native form-control rendering) and reads the filled values back out. The
output is meant to be handed off to an e-signature service such as DocuSign.

## Build, test, run

Use the committed Maven wrapper — there is no global `mvn` on the target machines, and the
wrapper pins the Maven version.

```bash
./mvnw test        # compile + run all tests
./mvnw package     # build the jar
```

Run a single test class or method (surefire syntax):

```bash
./mvnw -Dtest=ContractFormReaderTest test
./mvnw -Dtest=ContractGeneratorTest#generatesPdfWithExpectedFillableFields test
```

`./mvnw package` also attaches an **executable worker uber-jar** (maven-shade-plugin, classifier
`worker`, `Main-Class` = `temporal.WorkerMain`): `target/contract-generator-*-worker.jar`. The
plain library jar is unaffected. `rockcraft pack` builds the OCI rock around that jar.

There is no linter configured; do not add one unless asked.

## Toolchain constraints

- **Java 25** is required (`maven.compiler.release=25` in `pom.xml`). Temurin 25 is what's tested.
- **openhtmltopdf 1.0.10 pulls in PDFBox 2.0.24.** The explicit `pdfbox` dependency in `pom.xml`
  is deliberately pinned to that exact version — keep them aligned when bumping either, or the
  AcroForm code will break at runtime.
- **`com.docusign:docusign-esign-java:6.8.0`** provides the DocuSign SDK models/clients used by
  the `docusign` package.
- **`com.fasterxml.jackson.core:jackson-databind`** (pinned via `jackson.version`, same as the
  version the DocuSign SDK resolves transitively) is declared explicitly because the
  `docusign.webhook` parser reads the inbound Connect JSON itself.
- **`io.temporal:temporal-sdk` (`temporal.version`)** powers the `temporal` worker package;
  `temporal-testing` is test-scope. `micrometer-registry-prometheus` is pinned to
  `micrometer.version` = Temporal's micrometer BOM version to avoid a version clash. Temporal's
  default payload converter is Jackson, so the DTO records serialize without extra config.

## Architecture

Two inverse pipelines, both fronted by `ContractGenerator` (the only public entry point):

```
generate:  ContractData ─▶ ContractTemplateEngine (Thymeleaf) ─▶ XHTML
                        ─▶ HtmlToPdfRenderer (openhtmltopdf) ─▶ PDF + AcroForm
                        ─▶ AcroFormPostProcessor (PDFBox) ─▶ byte[]

read:      byte[]/Path/InputStream ─▶ ContractFormReader (PDFBox) ─▶ Map<String,String>
```

Package `tech.aydin.contracts.generator`:
- `ContractGenerator` — facade; `generate(...)` and `readValues(...)`.
- `template.ContractTemplateEngine` — Thymeleaf in **XML mode** (templates must be well-formed XHTML).
- `render.HtmlToPdfRenderer` — openhtmltopdf render; registers the bundled font.
- `form.AcroFormPostProcessor` — validates field names, sets `NeedAppearances`, rejects duplicates.
- `form.ContractFormReader` — extracts field values from a filled PDF.
- `form.FieldNaming` — the field-name convention + validation.
- `model.ContractData` — immutable builder holding dynamic template values.

The fillable regions are **not** placed by anchor text or coordinates: they are ordinary HTML
form controls (`<input>`, `<textarea>`, checkbox, radio, `<select>`) in the template, whose
`name` attribute becomes the AcroForm field's fully-qualified name.

## Non-obvious conventions & gotchas

These are load-bearing; violating them fails at runtime, often without an obvious message.

- **Templates must be well-formed XHTML.** Thymeleaf runs in XML mode: namespaced root, all void
  elements self-closed (`<input ... />`, `<br/>`, `<meta ... />`).
- **Wrap all form controls in a `<form>` element.** openhtmltopdf silently drops any control with
  no enclosing `<form>`, producing a PDF with **no AcroForm** (and `getAcroForm(null)` returns null).
- **Text/textarea controls need a font-relative dimension** such as `min-width: 1em`. Without a
  font-relative unit, openhtmltopdf never resolves the control's font and throws
  `NullPointerException: ... "spec" is null` deep inside form processing.
- **A font must be registered** — openhtmltopdf ships no default font. `HtmlToPdfRenderer`
  registers the bundled `resources/fonts/Contract-Regular.ttf` (Open Sans, SIL OFL) under the
  family `ContractFont` (`HtmlToPdfRenderer.FONT_FAMILY`); templates must use that family.
- **Field names must satisfy `FieldNaming`**: start with a letter; only letters, digits, `.`,
  `_`, `-`. Dotted names (`party.name`) create a hierarchical field, so a parent node `party`
  exists in the field tree — it is a `PDNonTerminalField`, not a value.
- **Always use PDFBox `getAcroForm(null)`**, never `getAcroForm()`. The no-arg overload runs a
  fixup that rebuilds/alters the form generated by openhtmltopdf. This is used consistently in
  both `AcroFormPostProcessor` and `ContractFormReader`.
- **Checkbox values must be read from the raw `/V` COS name, not `PDCheckBox.getValue()`.**
  openhtmltopdf writes each checkbox's `/Opt` export-value array as a single empty string;
  PDFBox then treats the on-state as an index into that array and silently returns `""` for a
  checked box. `ContractFormReader` compares the raw `/V` name to the on-appearance state instead
  and normalizes checkboxes to `"true"`/`"false"`. Preserve this workaround.
- **`ContractFormReader` returns terminal fields only** and returns an **empty map** (never
  throws) for a PDF with no AcroForm.

## Signatures / DocuSign

`tech.aydin.contracts.generator.docusign` sends the generated PDF to DocuSign for signature
via the official `docusign-esign-java` SDK, using **JWT Grant** auth and tab **auto-detection**
(`Document.transformPdfFields=true` — no manual tab placement/coordinates).

- **Pure / unit-tested (no network):** `EnvelopeFactory` (builds the SDK `EnvelopeDefinition`
  from a `SendRequest`) and `DocuSignSender` (facade; tested with a fake `DocuSignClient`).
- **Network I/O, integration-tested only:** `JwtAuthenticator` (JWT auth, resolves the account's
  REST base path via the userinfo endpoint) and `EsignDocuSignClient` (calls
  `EnvelopesApi.createEnvelope`). Exercised by `DocuSignLiveIntegrationTest`, which is skipped
  unless `DOCUSIGN_LIVE_TEST=true` and the other `DOCUSIGN_*` env vars are set (see its Javadoc).
- **Required fields, in both places:** `ContractGenerator.generate(..., expectedFieldNames,
  requiredFieldNames)` sets the AcroForm Required flag via `AcroFormPostProcessor`. Because
  `EnvelopeFactory` always sets `transformPdfFields=true`, DocuSign's auto-converted tabs inherit
  that required attribute — one flag drives both the PDF and the DocuSign tab.
- **Multi-signer caveat:** auto-detected tabs are all assigned to the first signer unless field
  names encode the recipient. Single-signer envelopes are the supported path; this is documented,
  not solved.
- Out of scope by design: non-JWT auth flows, explicit per-tab placement, embedded signing
  (recipient views), DocuSign Connect webhooks for *sending*, envelope status polling.

## Receiving signed docs (`docusign.webhook`)

Package `tech.aydin.contracts.generator.docusign.webhook` parses the **inbound** DocuSign
Connect notification back into form values — the inverse of the send pipeline.

- `ConnectWebhookParser.parse(byte[]/String)` → `SignedEnvelope(envelopeId, status, documents)`;
  each `SignedDocument` carries `pdfBytes` + parsed `fields`. It reuses `form.ContractFormReader`
  to read the AcroForm values, so all the reader's conventions (checkbox `/V` quirk, terminal
  fields only, empty map for no-AcroForm) apply to `SignedDocument.fields()`.
- **Only the JSON eSignature Connect format is parsed.** The base64 PDF lives at
  `data.envelopeSummary.envelopeDocuments[].PDFBytes` — note this is **`PDFBytes`** in the Connect
  payload, *not* `documentBase64` as in the SDK's `EnvelopeDocument` model. The SDK has no inbound
  deserializer, so we walk the JSON tree with Jackson ourselves.
- **Parse-regardless-of-status:** a notification without documents (not completed, or "Include
  Documents" off) parses into an empty `documents` list rather than throwing; only malformed JSON /
  a missing `data` object raises `WebhookParseException`. The completion certificate ("summary"
  document) has no form and yields empty fields.
- `ConnectHmacVerifier.verify/verifyAny` is a pure HMAC-SHA256 constant-time check of the **raw**
  request body against the Connect HMAC secret (`X-DocuSign-Signature-N` header). Verify before
  parsing; never re-serialize the body first.
- Out of scope: legacy XML Connect payloads, fetching documents from the API when the webhook
  omits them, and the HTTP endpoint/routing itself (caller's responsibility).

## Temporal worker & rock (`temporal`)

Package `tech.aydin.contracts.generator.temporal` wraps the library as a Temporal worker,
packaged as an OCI rock for the `temporal-worker-k8s` charm (2.0/stable). The workflow takes a
template name + parameters, generates the PDF, then sends it to DocuSign.

- `ContractSigningWorkflow.generateAndSend(ContractSigningRequest)` → envelope id. Impl orchestrates
  two activities (`ContractActivities`): `generatePdf` (wraps `ContractGenerator`) then
  `sendToDocuSign` (wraps `DocuSignSender`). PDF bytes pass between them through workflow history
  (base64) — fine under Temporal's ~2 MB payload limit.
- DTOs are Jackson-friendly records: `ContractSigningRequest`, `SignerInfo`. Their canonical
  constructors normalize null collections to empty copies.
- `TemporalWorkerConfig.fromEnv(Map)` reads `TEMPORAL_HOST`/`_NAMESPACE`/`_QUEUE`/`_TLS_ROOT_CAS`
  (queue required; host/namespace defaulted). `ContractActivitiesImpl` builds `DocuSignConfig`
  from `DOCUSIGN_*` env (`DOCUSIGN_PRIVATE_KEY` inline or `DOCUSIGN_PRIVATE_KEY_PATH`).
- `WorkerMain` is the shaded jar's entry point: stubs (TLS from `TEMPORAL_TLS_ROOT_CAS` via
  gRPC-shaded netty `GrpcSslContexts`), client, factory; optional Prometheus `/metrics` on
  `TEMPORAL_PROMETHEUS_PORT` (note `reportEvery` wants `com.uber.m3.util.Duration`, not
  `java.time.Duration`).
- Tests: `TemporalWorkerConfigTest` (pure env parsing), `ContractSigningWorkflowTest`
  (`TestWorkflowEnvironment` + fake activities asserting generate→send ordering),
  `ContractActivitiesImplTest` (`generatePdf` on the bundled template).
- Rock: `rockcraft.yaml` (`base`/`build-base` `ubuntu@26.04` → OpenJDK 25 via apt) + inject
  `rock/start-worker.sh` at `/app/scripts/start-worker.sh` (the charm's Pebble command). Bundled
  templates travel inside the jar, so `templateName` resolves from the classpath.
- **Out of scope** (temporal-lib-py extras): candid/google/OIDC auth, encryption codec, Sentry,
  Vault — extension points only.

## When adding fields

Adding a control to `templates/contract.html` is a cross-file change: update the template, and
if a test asserts the expected field set (see `EXPECTED_FIELDS` in `ContractGeneratorTest`) or
round-trips values (`ContractFormReaderTest`), update those too.
